issues.claim: Прогнать анализ .NET Upgrade Assistant по решению ... Upgrade Assistant автоматизирует механическую часть
issues.problem: The fetched upgrade-assistant-overview page says '.NET Upgrade Assistant is officially deprecated' and points to the GitHub Copilot modernization agent (Visual Studio 2026 or VS 2022 17.14.16+). The answer recommends the deprecated tool as the assessment and conversion tool, so a candidate would learn outdated tooling. The generator's own note flagged this risk.
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite the assessment step and the explanation to say that the .NET Upgrade Assistant is deprecated. Name the GitHub Copilot modernization chat agent, which analyses projects and dependencies and produces a migration plan, as the current tool. Keep the point that tools do the mechanical part but do not replace removed technologies or find behaviour differences. Change the first link title and URL to match, or cite the page only for the deprecation notice.

issues.claim: .NET 8 - LTS с поддержкой до 10 ноября 2026 года ... версия, поддержка которой заканчивается через несколько месяцев
issues.problem: The link excerpts are fetched on 2026-11-19, after the stated .NET 8 end-of-support date of 10 November 2026. The answer treats that date as upcoming ('ends within months'), but .NET 8 is already out of support at the time of verification. The dates themselves are correct. The framing is stale and the answer misses the strongest argument: do not target an unsupported runtime. The excerpt of the support policy page does not show the version table, so the dates rest on my own knowledge.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the text date-neutral or correct for the verification date. For example: '.NET 8 end of support is 10 November 2026, so a .NET 8 target is already out of support or about to be; .NET 10 (LTS, supported until November 2028) is the sensible target.' Change the explanation sentence to 'a version that is out of support or about to leave support requires the next move almost immediately'. Do the same in EN. Alternatively, tell the lead to push back on the .NET 8 target.
